sources.title: Macquarie University: Seringapatam 1799, introduction
sources.note: Direct university introduction to original Macquarie manuscripts read: island capital, 1792 territorial loss, 1799 Anglo-Indian campaign and May 4 capture. Does not adopt the page’s oversimplified claim that this immediately secured all southern India or its disputed Tipu birth date.

sources.title: Hassan District, Government of Karnataka: History
sources.note: Direct official district history read: Mysore became a princely state under British power after 1799; post-1947 transition. Used only for these political transitions, not legendary beginnings or unrelated numerical claims.

sources.title: National Army Museum: Tipu Sultan’s war turban
sources.note: Direct museum object study read: War turban, Guard, Provenance, Cornwallis and Colonel Floyd, Seringapatam prize. Textile structure and documented 1799 transfer; 1792 hostage princes. No claim that magical protection was effective.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum: Tipu’s Tiger
sources.note: Direct museum article read. Royal wooden automaton and tiger motifs; Haidar Ali and Tipu, Persian court language. URL is reused by the East India Company card, so cumulative runtime budget is checked.

sources.title: V&A: The Tiger and the Queen, a bust of Marie Antoinette from Tipu’s court
sources.note: Direct museum provenance study read, French Court and Third Anglo-Mysore War sections. Embassy arrived Paris July 16, 1788; factory visit, porcelain gifts, no formal military alliance. Avoid assuming exact uncertain route by which the surviving bust reached collector Rice.

sources.title: Francis Buchanan: A Journey from Madras through Mysore, Canara and Malabar, volume I (1807)
sources.note: Original public-domain book OCR downloaded directly and locally read in buchanan-original.txt. Printed pp.61-62 aqueduct bridge; p.102 ragi preparation; p.135 fuel trade. Observations made in 1800, after conquest; author’s prejudiced judgments about hygiene, women and technological ability explicitly excluded. Entire volume counted as one source.

sources.title: Sotheby’s: Thomas Hickey, Portrait of Three Princesses from Mysore, lot 45 (2007)
sources.note: Direct original object catalogue read. Catalogue Note dates painting circa 1805, summarizes competing sitter identifications and Nigel Chancellor’s 2001 vaccination interpretation; left arm, not right. Public wording preserves interpretation, and does not assert precise sitter names or universal vaccination.

sources.title: Roddam Narasimha: Rockets in Mysore and Britain, 1750-1850 AD (1985)
sources.note: Original National Aeronautical Laboratory/IISc research report, DU 8503, full 47-page PDF read at author-associated repository. PDF pages 6-7 describe hammered soft-iron casing and bamboo; page 13 British development from Indian reports and recovered cases. No claim Mysore invented all rockets, no adoption of speculative maximum range.

sources.title: Royal Collection Trust: al-Quran, RCIN 1005001
sources.note: Direct institutional catalogue 65 read. Manuscript made 1613 with late-eighteenth-century additions for Tipu, Persian tables, naskh, protective envelope flap and gold flowers. Clearly separates older manuscript from Tipu’s later use.

sources.title: Monopolizing Knowledge: The Roots of Company Science in Asia, chapter 2
sources.note: Direct open scholarly chapter, printed pp.34-35 / PDF pages 1-2; Buchanan’s botanical notebook was mistakenly packed by colleague in 1785, taken in 1790, rebound in Tipu’s library, recovered after conquest and returned by Major Ogg. Does not quote primary diary at length.

sources.title: J. R. Henderson: The Coins of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan (Madras Government Museum, 1921)
sources.note: Original government museum catalogue, direct full PDF and local file. Printed p.16 / PDF page 32 visually inspected (coin-p16.png): first-type ahmadi, obverse Hijri 1198 and reverse regnal year 2; opening Arabic هو / السلطان and author’s English translation. Printed p.15 discusses gold denominations and multiple mints. Only a short unambiguous excerpt used; no reliance on garbled Arabic OCR.

proposedOverrides.name: Mysore
proposedOverrides.summary: Southern Indian power, then a restored Wodeyar kingdom under British supremacy.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Only this exact indexed ID attached. Two imported outlines span 1783-1800 and 1800-1815, both retain extensive southern territory; western edge changes only slightly. Do not validate these as the actual post-1792 or post-1799 frontiers. Public overview explicitly warns partition mismatch. Narrative distinguishes Haidar/Tipu independent power from restored Wodeyar state under Company supremacy, and labels 1800 household observations and circa 1805 portrait accordingly. Imported dates retained as map_coverage. No claim that 1815 ended the kingdom; no exact historical founding invented.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Contemporary coin Arabic, not vernacular Kannada. Excerpt visually verified in government museum catalogue, no Arabic reconstructed from OCR.
